blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A reporting module declares `public abstract sealed class Report permits DailyReport, MonthlyReport`, then `public final class MonthlyReport extends Report` and `public class DailyReport extends Report`. The build fails at DailyReport. Other teams in the module must be able to write their own subclasses of DailyReport. Which change does that?

options.text: Add `final` to DailyReport, since in a sealed hierarchy final keeps out only classes from other modules
options.says: final ends the branch: no class at all can extend DailyReport

options.text: Add `non-sealed` to DailyReport, since that lets classes the permits lists don't name extend it
options.says: the page: non-sealed means anyone may extend this class, as the partner's GiftWallet extended Wallet

options.text: Add `sealed` to DailyReport with no permits clause, since that lets every class in the module extend it
options.says: a sealed class keeps its branch closed, and one without permitted subclasses fails with 'sealed class must have subclasses'

options.text: Add `abstract` to DailyReport, since an abstract permitted class needs no other modifier to be extended
options.says: abstract is not one of the three choices; javac still reports 'sealed, non-sealed or final modifiers expected'

origin.section: Every Permitted Subclass Says Whether the Hierarchy Goes On: final, sealed or non-sealed

questions.stem: `sealed interface Command permits Start, Stop, Plugin`: Start and Stop are records, and `Plugin` is a `non-sealed abstract class` with an abstract `run()`. The dispatcher has `switch (cmd) { case Start s -> ...; case Stop s -> ...; case Plugin p -> p.run(); }` with no default. A separate jar later adds `class ReloadPlugin extends Plugin`. A ReloadPlugin reaches the dispatcher, which was not rebuilt. What happens, and what happens when the dispatcher is rebuilt?

options.text: The Plugin case runs it, and the rebuild compiles, since a ReloadPlugin is matched as a Plugin
options.says: the gift wallet ran the Wallet case; every subtype of a non-sealed class is an instance of it, so the switch stays exhaustive

options.text: The Plugin case runs it, but the rebuild fails, since ReloadPlugin needs a case of its own
options.says: the switch is still exhaustive: the Plugin case covers every subclass of Plugin, known or not

options.text: MatchException is thrown, but the rebuild compiles, since ReloadPlugin then matches as a Plugin
options.says: MatchException is for a type added to a permits list; a subclass of a non-sealed class matches that class's case without a rebuild

options.text: MatchException is thrown, and the rebuild fails, since the switch now misses one subtype of Command
options.says: neither: the Plugin case takes it, and a switch over the sealed root is exhaustive with or without ReloadPlugin

origin.section: non-sealed Reopens One Branch, and Subtypes Nobody Listed Arrive Through Its Case

questions.stem: There is no module-info.java, and the application runs from the classpath. Package `com.acme.orders` has `public sealed interface OrderEvent permits com.acme.orders.audit.AuditedOrder`, and package `com.acme.orders.audit` has `public final class AuditedOrder implements com.acme.orders.OrderEvent`. What does javac do with this code?

options.text: It compiles, since in the unnamed module a subpackage counts as the same package
options.says: javac compares packages exactly; com.acme.orders.audit is a different package from com.acme.orders

options.text: It compiles, since in the unnamed module any public class may be permitted
options.says: that holds for the JVM's load-time check, not for javac, which requires the sealed type's package

options.text: It reports an error, since in the unnamed module the two classes must share a package
options.says: the page's run: 'in unnamed module cannot extend a sealed class in a different package'

options.text: It reports an error, since in the unnamed module a permitted class must not be public
options.says: permitted classes may be public, like the page's Wallet; the error is the different package

origin.section: Permitted Subclasses Live in the Sealed Type's Module, or in Its Package When There Is No Module

questions.stem: The shapes library declares `sealed interface Shape permits Polygon, Circle {}`, `sealed class Polygon implements Shape permits Triangle, Quad {}`, `final class Triangle extends Polygon {}`, `final class Quad extends Polygon {}` and `record Circle(double r) implements Shape {}`. A method returns `switch (shape) { case Triangle t -> 3; case Quad q -> 4; case Circle c -> 0; }` with no default. What does javac do with this code?

options.text: It compiles, since the cases for Triangle and Quad together cover every Polygon
options.says: Polygon isn't abstract, so a value can be a Polygon itself, which neither case matches

options.text: It compiles, since the compiler treats the sealed Polygon as just Triangle and Quad
options.says: the permitted classes cover a sealed class only when it is abstract or an interface

options.text: It reports an error, since a Polygon that is neither a Triangle nor a Quad has no case
options.says: the page's run: 'the switch expression does not cover all possible input values' until Polygon is abstract or has its own case

options.text: It reports an error, since the cases for Triangle and Quad don't count toward covering Shape
options.says: they do count: an abstract Polygon would be covered by them without a case of its own

origin.section: A sealed Subclass Keeps the Set Closed, but a Switch Needs a Case for It Unless It Is Abstract

concepts: A permitted subclass must declare final, sealed or non-sealed; javac has no default and reports the subclass that declares none.
A switch over the sealed root stays exhaustive with a case for the non-sealed type, and every unknown subtype of it runs that case, with no compile error and no MatchException.
Permitted subclasses must be in the sealed type's named module, or in its package when it is in the unnamed module.
A switch over the root covers a sealed subclass through its permitted subclasses only when it is abstract or an interface; otherwise the switch needs a case for it.
